ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, block A with mass $M=2\sqrt{3}\mathrm{kg}$ is placed on a horizontal rod and connected to a small ball with mass $m=\sqrt{3}\mathrm{kg}$ by a light rope. A force $F=10\sqrt{3}\mathrm{N}$ is applied at an angle $\alpha=30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, pulling the ball and causing block A to move to the right at a constant velocity. During the motion, the relative positions of $M$ and $m$ remain unchanged. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. During the motion, the angle $\theta$ between the light rope and the horizontal direction
2. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the wooden block and the horizontal rod is $\mu$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the wooden block M is located on the horizontal rod on the left, and the string is obliquely connected from the wooden block to the small ball m toward the lower right; the angle θ is marked between the string and the horizontal rod. On the right side of the small ball there is an arrow of external force F, directed toward the upper right, and making 30° with the horizontal dashed line at the small ball. The relative positions of the wooden block and the small ball do not change during the motion, and the whole moves uniformly to the right, so the forces on each object can be treated according to equilibrium. Reasoning: First write the equilibrium equations for the small ball. The small ball is subject to three forces: tension T along the string pointing to the upper left, external force F to the upper right with α=30°, and gravity mg downward. Equilibrium in the horizontal direction: F cos α = T cos θ. Equilibrium in the vertical direction: F sin α + T sin θ = mg. Substitute F=10√3 N, m=√3 kg, g=10 m/s², α=30°: mg=10√3 N, F cos30°=10√3·√3/2=15 N, F sin30°=5√3 N. Therefore T cosθ=15, T sinθ=10√3-5√3=5√3. Dividing the two equations: tanθ=(T sinθ)/(T cosθ)=5√3/15=√3/3, so θ=30°. Then write the equilibrium equations for the wooden block. The tension of the string on the wooden block is along the string toward the lower right, with components T cosθ to the right and T sinθ downward; gravity Mg downward, normal force N upward; the wooden block moves uniformly to the right, and kinetic friction μN is to the left. Equilibrium in the horizontal direction: μN=T cosθ. Equilibrium in the vertical direction: N=Mg+T sinθ. From above, T cosθ=15 and T sinθ=5√3 have been obtained; also M=2√3 kg, so Mg=20√3 N. Thus N=20√3+5√3=25√3 N, μ=15/(25√3)=√3/5.
